assumptions.assumption: Events with a NULL status form their own group, since GROUP BY keeps NULLs as a group. The request does not say whether to drop them.
The denominator is the sum of the per-status distinct-member counts. A member who attended events with several different statuses is counted once in each status, as the request specifies.

responses.sql: WITH per_status AS (SELECT e.status AS status, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS member_count FROM attendance a JOIN event e ON e.event_id = a.link_to_event GROUP BY e.status) SELECT status, member_count, CAST(member_count AS REAL) / SUM(member_count) OVER () AS proportion FROM per_status

assumptions.assumption: Events with a NULL status form their own group, since GROUP BY keeps NULLs as a group and they are included in the denominator.

The denominator is the sum of the per-status distinct member counts. A member who attended events with several statuses is counted once in each status, so the proportions sum to 1 across statuses. The denominator is not the number of distinct members overall.

responses.sql: WITH per_status AS (SELECT e.status AS status, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS member_count FROM attendance a JOIN event e ON e.event_id = a.link_to_event GROUP BY e.status) SELECT status, member_count, CAST(member_count AS REAL) / SUM(member_count) OVER () AS proportion FROM per_status

assumptions.assumption: Events with a NULL status form their own group (GROUP BY keeps NULL as a group) and are included in the denominator; in practice status is expected to be Open/Closed/Planning.
The ratio is returned as a floating-point fraction (not a percentage), unrounded.
